newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cyprus population almost doubles since 1960.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cyprus population almost doubles since 1960.

text.p: The population of Turks living on the divided island of Cyprus has almost doubled in the last 36 years, Turkish Cypriot officials said on Thursday.

They said the number of people counted in the census this month in the self-declared Turkish Cypriot state in the north was 198,000, up from 104,000 Turkish Cypriots in 1960 when the island gained independence from Britain.

Turkish Cypriot officials would not give a breakdown of the number of Turks compared with Turkish Cypriots in the north, which broke away from the Greek Cypriots in 1974 when Turkey invaded after a coup on the island engineered by the military regime then ruling Greece.

Since the division, tens of thousands of mainland Turks have settled in the breakaway state. The Cyprus government, which is based in the south, says this is a deliberate attempt to change the island's demography.
Turkey's 30,000 troops stationed in the north were not included in the count.
"The economic, social and demographic analysis results will be available in detail after out technicians (visit) the state statistical department in Turkey," statistician Zeki Buluc told reporters.
A 1994 Cypriot government census showed there were 623,200 Greek Cypriots on the island and an estimated 90,600 Turkish Cypriots plus about 23,000 others.
Small Maronite Christian communities live on both sides of the island's U.N.-patrolled Green Line and there is also a small number of Armenians in the south.
